BUS.G11.T2.PROFETHICS.A1.title: Professionalism & ethics
BUS.G11.T2.PROFETHICS.A1.description: The theories and principles of professionalism and ethics and how they relate to business: the definitions and differences between them, good vs bad decisions, the concept of ethics and different perspectives, and the skills of professional, responsible, ethical and effective business practice.
BUS.G11.T2.PROFETHICS.A1.strand: T2 — Creative thinking, stress & change, action plans, setting up, ethics & presentation
BUS.G11.T2.PROFETHICS.A1.recovery_strategy: Ethics = doing what is morally right (honest, fair). Professionalism = the standard of conduct in your work (reliable, respectful, competent). You can be professional and still face an ethical choice; the two support each other.

questions.question: What is ethics mainly about?
options: Doing what is morally right and fair
Making the most profit by any means
questions.expected: Doing what is morally right and fair
questions.memo: Ethics is about choosing what is morally right and fair, even when another choice might be easier or more profitable.

questions.question: What is professionalism mainly about?
options: The standard of conduct and competence in your work
questions.expected: The standard of conduct and competence in your work
questions.memo: Professionalism is the standard of behaviour and skill in your work — being reliable, respectful and competent.

questions.question: Honesty and fairness in business are part of business _________.
questions.memo: Honesty and fairness are core to business ethics — acting in morally right ways.

questions.question: True or false: Professionalism and ethics mean exactly the same thing.
questions.memo: They are related but different: ethics is about right and wrong; professionalism is about the standard of conduct in your work.

questions.question: True or false: Paying workers a fair wage is an example of ethical business practice.
questions.memo: Paying fair wages treats employees justly, which is ethical business behaviour.

questions.question: Arriving on time, prepared and reliable mainly shows _________.
questions.memo: Being punctual, prepared and dependable is professional conduct.

questions.question: Sort each example into whether it mainly shows professionalism or ethics.

items.text: Arriving on time and dressing appropriately
Replying to emails promptly and politely
Telling a customer the truth about a faulty product
Paying suppliers fairly and on time

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Conduct and competence (punctuality, preparation, politeness) is professionalism; doing what is morally right (honesty, fairness, refusing bribes) is ethics.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of UNETHICAL business practice?
options: Paying a bribe to win a contract
questions.expected: Paying a bribe to win a contract
questions.memo: Bribery is dishonest and unfair — clearly unethical. The other options are ethical practices.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of UNPROFESSIONAL behaviour?
options: Arriving late and unprepared for a client meeting
questions.expected: Arriving late and unprepared for a client meeting
questions.memo: Turning up late and unprepared falls below the expected standard of conduct, so it is unprofessional.

questions.question: Build a 3-part explanation of why ethical behaviour matters for a business.
questions.prompt: Build a 3-part explanation of why ethical behaviour matters for a business.

options.text: Ethical behaviour matters because it builds trust with customers and staff
Ethical behaviour matters because it lets a business break the law safely
Ethical behaviour matters only when no one is watching
Customers return to and recommend businesses they believe are honest and fair
Customers prefer businesses that cheat them
Staff work harder for employers who treat them unfairly
A trusted reputation attracts loyal customers and good staff, supporting long-term success
A bad reputation has no effect on a business
Ethics only matters to charities, not businesses

questions.memo: Claim: ethics builds trust. Evidence: people support honest, fair businesses. Explanation: a trusted reputation brings loyal customers and good staff, helping long-term success.

questions.question: An _________ decision weighs what is right and fair, not only what is most profitable.
questions.memo: An ethical decision considers fairness and the effect on others, not just the profit it brings.

questions.question: True or false: Acting ethically can build customer trust and a good reputation.
questions.memo: When a business is consistently honest and fair, customers trust it and its reputation grows, which supports success.

questions.question: Sort each practice into ethical or unethical.

items.text: Paying all taxes that are due

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Honest advertising, paying tax and safe conditions are ethical; selling expired goods, taking kickbacks and misleading on price are unethical.

questions.question: What makes a 'good' business decision different from a 'bad' one?
options: A good decision considers the consequences and fairness, not just short-term gain
A good decision always ignores other people
A good decision is simply the fastest one
A good decision is whatever makes the most money today
questions.expected: A good decision considers the consequences and fairness, not just short-term gain
questions.memo: Good decisions weigh the effects on others and fairness, while bad decisions chase short-term gain regardless of the harm caused.

questions.question: Which is a skill of ethical, responsible business practice?
options: Being honest and transparent in dealings
questions.expected: Being honest and transparent in dealings
questions.memo: Honesty and transparency are key skills of ethical, responsible business practice.

questions.question: Different _________ on ethics means people may judge what is right or wrong differently.
questions.memo: People hold different perspectives on ethics, so the same action may be judged differently depending on values and context.

questions.question: A manager can win a contract by lying about the product's quality. What does ethical business practice require?
options: Telling the truth, even if it means losing the contract
Lying, because winning is all that matters
Hiding the truth and hoping no one finds out
Blaming a junior employee for any complaints
questions.expected: Telling the truth, even if it means losing the contract
questions.memo: Ethical practice means being honest even when it costs the business, because trust and integrity matter more than one contract.

questions.question: Why does professionalism support ethical behaviour at work?
options: Professional standards like honesty, respect and accountability make ethical conduct part of daily work
Professionalism replaces the need for any ethics
questions.expected: Professional standards like honesty, respect and accountability make ethical conduct part of daily work
questions.memo: A professional standard built on honesty, respect and accountability naturally encourages and supports ethical behaviour.

questions.question: Why might two people disagree about whether a business decision is ethical?
options: They hold different values and perspectives on what is right
Ethics is a fixed mathematical formula
One of them must be lying
questions.expected: They hold different values and perspectives on what is right
questions.memo: Because people bring different values and perspectives, they can reach different conclusions about the same ethical question.

questions.question: An employee notices the company is overcharging vulnerable customers. What is the most ethical and professional response?
options: Raise the concern through the proper channels so it can be corrected
Say nothing because it boosts profit
Quietly overcharge a few more customers
Tell customers to complain on social media anonymously first
questions.expected: Raise the concern through the proper channels so it can be corrected
questions.memo: The ethical and professional path is to raise the issue responsibly through the right channels so the unfair practice is stopped.
